question: In a 45-year-old adult presenting with unilateral serous otitis media, flexible nasendoscopy to exclude a nasopharyngeal mass is mandatory before any other management.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This is a critical safety rule: adult unilateral OME demands exclusion of nasopharyngeal carcinoma by flexible nasendoscopy FIRST. Treating it with a grommet without nasendoscopy risks missing an NPC diagnosis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Unilateral OME in an adult is a red flag. Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) can obstruct the Eustachian tube orifice in the fossa of Rosenmuller and present exactly as unilateral OME. Nasendoscopy is mandatory — insertion of a grommet without this step can dangerously delay an NPC diagnosis.
